title: Common Phrasal Verbs
explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs combined with a particle (preposition or adverb) that changes the meaning. They are extremely common in everyday English. Many have meanings that are not obvious from the individual words.
examples: give up = stop trying / quit → Don't give up! Keep practicing.
look forward to = be excited about something in the future → I look forward to meeting you.
run out of = have no more left → We ran out of milk.
turn down = reject / lower volume → She turned down the job offer.
come up with = think of / invent → He came up with a great idea.

exercises.question: I need to ___ (stop trying). This is too hard!
exercises.explanation: 'Give up' means to stop trying or quit.

exercises.question: We've ___ (have no more) sugar. Can you buy some?
exercises.explanation: 'Run out of' means to have no more of something left.

exercises.question: She ___ (thought of) a brilliant solution to the problem.
exercises.explanation: 'Come up with' means to think of or invent something.

exercises.question: I really ___ (am excited about) the weekend.
exercises.explanation: 'Look forward to' means to be excited about something in the future.

exercises.question: The company ___ (rejected) his application.
exercises.explanation: 'Turn down' means to reject or refuse something.
